why: Not everything a pub sings has a chart row. Two of the sources on the brief, the ARIA Hall of Fame and the Spicks and Specks style pub singalong, are not lists of songs at all, so they were tested by hand: 85 songs a Gold Coast room would sing without being asked were checked against the library one at a time. 77 of the 85 were already there, which is the real finding. These are the ones that were not. Advance Australia Fair was checked and deliberately left out: the anthem is not a bingo square. A second group was added the same day: 50 songs that were kept out of the 9 September run only because the library already held that title by another act. The card shows the title and nothing else, so both versions can sit in the library without confusing anybody.
how_they_were_checked: Every ARIA Hall of Fame inductee linked on the Wikipedia page was matched against the library. Only three performing acts had no song at all: The Masters Apprentices, The Loved Ones and The Dingoes. The rest of this list is the Countdown era and pub singalong test.

excluded.why: These cleared the chart bar and were still kept out. Each one is a judgement call, written down so it can be argued with.
acts: Rolf Harris. Convicted of child sex offences. No Australian venue wants his face on the TV, whatever the 1960 chart says.
Gary Glitter. The same, and his records are effectively unplayable on Australian radio.
songs: A Scottish Soldier, Andy Stewart. The 9 September run named this one as the example of a chart topper that is not a musical bingo square, and nothing has changed.
My Boomerang Won't Come Back, Charlie Drake. A year-end number five in 1961 built on a racial caricature.
Advance Australia Fair. The anthem is not a bingo square.

note_on_years: The store's release date is the date of the album it served up, which for an old single is often a much later compilation: it dates The Loved One to 1985 and U2's One to 1988. Where that would put a song in the wrong decade pack the right year is pinned here and it wins.
